questions.question: Hawa Mahal is situated in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Location and Design:** Hawa Mahal, also known as the "Palace of Winds," is located in Jaipur, the capital city of Rajasthan, India.

 
 
• It was designed in the form of the crown of Lord Krishna, with its unique five-story exterior resembling a honeycomb.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance: **Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, Hawa Mahal is an architectural marvel that is an integral part of Jaipur's history and royal heritage.
 
 
• It was constructed to enable ladies of the royal household to watch the life and processions of the city without being seen from the outside, given the strict "purdah" system followed at that time.
 
 
 
• **Architecture:** Hawa Mahal is a prime example of Rajput architecture and Indian artistry with its pink sandstone construction.
 
 
• The building does not have a foundation, and it is the tallest building in the world that does not have a solid base. It has over 950 windows, known as 'Jharokhas,' decorated with intricate latticework.
 
 
 
• **Ventilation: **The name "Hawa Mahal" translates to "Palace of Winds," which refers to the natural ventilation system in the building.
 
 
• The unique design of the windows allows cool air to circulate naturally through the building, making it an early example of sustainable architecture.
 
 
 
• **Tourism: **Today, Hawa Mahal is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Jaipur. Visitors can climb to the top floor for a panoramic view of the city, including the Jantar Mantar and the City Palace on one side and the Siredeori Bazaar on the other.
 
 
• It's a great place to learn about the culture and history of Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:** The Hawa Mahal is maintained by the Archaeological Department of the Government of Rajasthan.
 
 
• The monument is well-preserved, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the region, despite being over two centuries old.

questions.question: Who among the following is the Union Minister for Tribal Affairs as on October 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Shri Arjun Munda is the **Union Minister for Tribal Affairs as on October 2022.**
 
• **The Ministry of Tribal Affairs** in India is a federal authority that is responsible for the overall welfare of tribal communities. **The Union Minister for Tribal Affairs **holds a significant role in shaping and implementing policies for these communities. Here are four key responsibilities:
 
 
• **Policy Development and Implementation: **The Union Minister is responsible for formulating and executing policies, plans, and programs for the socio-economic development of the Scheduled Tribes (STs) in India. This includes legislative and administrative measures that aim to bridge the development gap between STs and the rest of the population.
 
• **Promotion of Education: **One of the crucial responsibilities is the promotion and enhancement of educational opportunities for tribal communities. The minister oversees programs and initiatives that encourage and support education among STs, such as the Eklavya Model Residential Schools and Post-Matric Scholarship for ST students.
 
• **Preservation of Cultural Heritage: **The minister has the duty to preserve and promote the rich heritage, culture, and languages of the tribal communities. This involves backing initiatives that foster cultural exchange and understanding, support traditional arts and crafts, and safeguard tribal cultures and traditions.
 
• **Liaison with Other Ministries and Departments: **The Union Minister often works closely with other ministries and departments at both the central and state levels to ensure that the welfare measures reach the tribal communities effectively. This involves coordinating with departments like Health, Education, Rural Development, and others to synchronize their efforts towards tribal development.

questions.question: Who wrote the "Harshacharita", a biography of Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banabhatta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The "**Harshacharita**", a biography of Harshavardhana, was written by Banabhatta, who was a **Sanskrit scholar **and a poet in the court of Harshavardhana. Banabhatta lived around the** 7th century CE**.
 
• "**Harshacharita**" is a historical narrative detailing the life and times of King Harsha, who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE. 
 
• He is also known for his work "**Kadambari.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harisena:**

 
 
• He was a court poet of **Samudragupta**, a Gupta emperor.
 
• His most notable work is the** Allahabad Pillar Inscription**, which details the conquests and accomplishments of his patron.
 
 
 
• **Ravikirti:**
 
 
• He was the court poet of the Chalukya king **Pulakeshin II**.
 
• His work, the** Aihole Prashasti **(Aihole Inscription), written in Sanskrit, extols the victory of Pulakeshin II over the northern king Harshavardhana.
 
 
 
• **Xuan Zang:**
 
 
• He was a **Chinese Buddhist monk**, scholar, traveler, and translator who traveled to India in the 7th century.
 
• His works, "**Great Tang Records on the Western Regions**" and "**Buddhist Records of the Western World**," detail his journey and experiences in India and other parts of Central and South Asia.

questions.question: What is an output device that transforms the signal from the computer's sound card into audio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A speaker is an output device that transforms digital signals processed by the computer's sound card into **audible sound waves **or **audio**.
 
• The sound card sends an electrical signal to the speaker, and then the speaker converts this electrical signal into physical vibrations (**sound waves**) that we can hear.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Device
 Input/Output Device
 Function / Signal Conversion
 
 
 
 

 Plotter
 Output
 Plotters convert digital vector images sent from the computer into physical plots on various materials, usually paper or plastic, using pens or other drawing instruments. The computer sends data to the plotter specifying the colors and shapes in the image, and the plotter then creates the image on the output medium.
 
 

 Graphics Card
 Output
 The graphics card takes digital visual data from the processor and converts it into a signal that the monitor can display. The resulting output is what you see on your monitor. The graphics card is vital for rendering high-quality images quickly, especially for video games and high-definition videos.
 
 

 Monitor
 Output
 The monitor receives digital or analog signals from the graphics card and converts them into visible light displays. In a nutshell, the graphics card translates the data into signals the monitor can use, and the monitor displays these signals as the images you see on the screen.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies equality before the law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 14**

 
 
• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution is about '**Equality Before Law**' and it states:
 
• "The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the** territory of India**."
 
• This article is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution of India, which talks about** Rights to Equality**.
 
• The principle of 'Equality before law' is of British origin, while 'Equal protection of the laws' is borrowed from the** Constitution of the United States**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Article
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Article 19
 
 
This article guarantees** six fundamental freedoms** to all citizens of India:

 
 
• Freedom of Speech and Expression,
 
• Freedom to Assemble Peaceably and Without Arms,
 
• Freedom to form Associations or Unions,
 
• Freedom to Move Freely Throughout the Territory of India,
 
• Freedom to Reside and Settle in Any Part of the Territory of India, and
 
• Freedom to Practice Any Profession, or to Carry on Any Occupation, Trade or Business. 
 
 
 
 

 Article 23
 
 
 
• Article 23 prohibits human trafficking, forced labour, and any form of exploitation. It states: "Traffic in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law." 
 
 
 
 

 Article 36
 
 
 
• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which are guidelines or directions given to the state for creating a social order characterized by justice – social, economic, and political. Article 36 defines the 'State' to include the government and Parliament of India and the government and legislatures of each of the states and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.

questions.question: Which Union Ministry implements the “Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0” scheme?

options.text: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Ministry of Health and Family welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Women and Child Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Saksham Anganwadi **and **Poshan 2.0** are part of the umbrella scheme "**Mission Shakti**" launched by the Government of India.
 
• These initiatives were introduced in the **Union Budget 2021-22 **with an aim to strengthen nutritional content, delivery, outreach, and outcomes with a focus on developing practices that nurture health and wellness.
 
• **Saksham Anganwadi**:
 
 
• This initiative is designed to **upgrade the Anganwadis **of India and turn them into more effective institutions for delivering public services to** women** and children.
 
• Anganwadi centers are rural mother and child care centers in India, established under the Integrated **Child Development Services** (ICDS) program to combat child hunger and malnutrition. "Saksham Anganwadi" aims to provide a digital solution to improve delivery outcomes with the use of technology.
 
• The plan is to develop** e-Anganwadi**, a digital platform to monitor and track the performance and growth of each Anganwadi.
 
 
 
• **Poshan 2.0**:
 
 
• Poshan Abhiyaan, also known as the** National Nutrition Mission**, was launched in **2018** to improve the nutritional status of children up to **6 years**, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• The mission aimed to reduce the level of stunting, undernutrition, anemia, and low birth weight babies. "**Poshan 2.0**" is a reboot or continuation of this mission with stronger strategies and improved implementation mechanisms.

questions.question: Plant cells differ from animal cells in having an additional layer around the cell membrane termed as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Cell wall.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The cell wall is present in plant cells but not in animal cells and it is made up of **cellulose and chitin.**
 
• The plant is covered by an outer cell wall.
 
• **Cellulose is one of the major components of the cell wall.**
 
• It is a polymer of glucose joined by glycosidic linkage.
 
• **It helps in maintaining its shape and provides rigidity to the plant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

**Mitochondria:**

 
• **Mitochondria is a double-layered cell organelle, **in which the outer layer is porous and the inner layer is folded upon itself is known to be **cristae.**
 
• The number of mitochondria in a single cell may be up to 50 to 5000.
 
• The inner lumen of mitochondria contains ribosome phosphate particles and** DNA **molecules.
 
• It has the potential to synthesize its own protein and the oxidation of carbohydrates and fats are taken place with the help of enzymes in mitochondria.
 
• This energy is stored in the form of **ATP **( Adenosine Triphosphate ) so, these are known as the "Powerhouse of the cell".

**Golgi apparatus:**

 
• **This cell organelle is primarily responsible for the storage, processing, and packaging of proteins.**
 
• Golgi Apparatus is found within the cytoplasm of a cell and are present in both plant and animal cells.

**Ribosomes:**

 
• The eukaryotic cell comprises of true nucleus and organelles in its cytoplasm.
 
• Mitochondria, ribosomes, Endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi complex are organelles present in the cytoplasm.
 
• **The sites for protein synthesis in the cells are ribosomes.**
 
• **Ribosomes are present as free ribosomes in the cytoplasm or, as membrane-bound on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
• Ribosomes consist of small and large subunits and are 80s-type.
 
• It is the site where **mRNA translation **occurs, and protein formation takes place.

questions.question: Which Union Ministry is related to Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?

options.text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a credit-linked subsidy program.
 
• It was launched in 2008 for the generation of employment opportunities through the establishment of microenterprises in rural and urban areas.
 
• It is a central sector scheme being administered by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME).
 
• Implementing Agency at the National Level is Khadi and Village Industries Commission(KVIC).
 
 
• It is a statutory organization under the administrative control of the Ministry of MSME.
 
 
 
• Features of the scheme are as follow-
 
 
• It allows entrepreneurs to set up factories or units.
 
• Any individual above 18 years of age is eligible for this scheme.
 
• Only new projects/units are considered for sanction of loans.
 
• Maximum Cost of Project/Unit Admissible for Manufacturing Sector is Rs. 50 lakh.
 
• Maximum Cost of Project/Unit Admissible for Service Sector is Rs. 20 lakh.
 
• The government has decided to provide Subsidy in Rural Areas - 25% for the general category and 35% for the special category, which includes SC/ST/ OBC/Minorities, Northeast Region, Hill, and Border Areas. and, In Urban Areas- 15% for general category and 25% for special categories.
 
• Under the scheme, loans are provided by Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Co-operative Banks, and Private Scheduled Commercial Banks approved by respective State Task Force Committee.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, a branch of the Government of India.
 
• It is the apex executive body for the formulation and administration of rules, regulations, and laws relating to micro, small and medium enterprises in India.

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct regarding the heating of the air?

I. It expands and occupies more space.

II. It becomes heavier on heating.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer ***Only I***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Statement I:** **When air is heated, it expands and occupies more space.**

 
• This phenomenon is a result of the increase in the kinetic energy of the air molecules.
 
• As the air molecules gain energy, they move more vigorously and spread out, leading to an increase in volume and expansion of the air.
 
• This expansion is commonly observed in various situations, such as hot air rising or the expansion of air in a balloon when it is exposed to heat.

**Statement II, which suggests that air becomes heavier on heating, is incorrect.**

 
• Heating air does not cause it to become heavier.
 
• In fact, as the air expands and occupies more space when heated, its density decreases, making it lighter compared to an equal volume of cooler air.
 
• This is why hot air tends to rise above cooler air in the atmosphere.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is an employment scheme that was launched in 2005 to provide social security by guaranteeing a minimum of ________ days of paid work per year to all families whose adult members opt for unskilled labour-intensive work.

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provide 100 days of guaranteed wage employment.
 
• This was initiated with the objective of “enhancing livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year, especially to households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work".
 
• This Act also aims to create durable assets (such as roads, canals, ponds, and wells).
 
• Within 5 km of an applicant’s residence, employment is provided.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**Objectives of MGNREGA:

• Provide 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to rural unskilled labour
 
• Increase economic security.
 
• Decrease migration of labour from rural to urban areas.
 
• It was known to be the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.
 
• MGNREGA Job Card is a document that renders a worker entitled to work under the MGNREGA scheme.

questions.question: India’s First open Rock Museum is located in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hyderabad__.

__
 
• Union Minister of State Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh inaugurated India’s first unique Rock Museum in Hyderabad.
 
• The Open Rock Museum has been set up with the aim to educate people about several lesser-known facts.
 
• It displays around 35 different types of rocks from different parts of India with ages ranging from 3.3 billion yrs to around 55 million years of the Earth’s history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

• It showcases approximately** 35 different types of rocks** sourced from** various regions in India.**
 
• These rocks not only represent a wide range of geological diversity but also include specimens that originate from the deepest parts of the Earth, reaching depths of up to 175 kilometers below the **Earth's surface.**
 
• The** museum exhibits rocks collected from different states** in India, such as **Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand, Jammu & Kashmir, **among others.
 
• **Each rock specimen is carefully selected to highlight its unique characteristics,** geological significance, and the processes that contributed to its formation over millions of years.

questions.question: When was the Lucknow Pact signed by All India Muslim League and Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1916**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lucknow Pact** was** signed by the All India Muslim League and the Indian National Congress in 1916.**
 
• **The Lucknow Pact was a significant event in the Indian National Movement.**
 
• It marked the reunion of the moderate and extremist factions of the Congress**, which had split in 1907.**
 
• This agreement brought the** Muslim League and the Indian National Congress closer.**
 
• **They agreed to work together to put pressure on the British Government to grant more political power to Indians.**
 
• The pact recognized separate electorates for Muslims in provinces where they were a minority, which was a significant demand of the Muslim League.
 
• The pact was also significant in that it proposed the **idea of granting more autonomy to the provinces, which eventually laid the groundwork for India's federal structure post-independence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Year
 Event
 
 
 
 

 1911
 
 
The 26th session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta.

 
It was presided by Bishan Narayan Dar.

 
This session opposed the partition of Bengal.

 
 
 

 1906
 
 
The 21st session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta. Dadabhai Naoroji, one of the founders of the Indian National Congress, presided over it.

 
This session was significant because it adopted 'Swaraj' (Self-rule) as the goal of the Indian National Congress.

 
 
 

 1919
 
 
The Indian National Congress, under the presidency of Motilal Nehru, committed itself to fight for dominion status and the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms were adopted.

 
In response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, the Congress initiated widespread protests.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam dance form gets its name from Hindu God ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishnu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, India.
 
• **The term "Mohiniyattam" translates to "dance of the enchantress."**
 
• The dance form gets its name from the Hindu God Vishnu.
 
• In Hindu mythology, **Mohini is a female avatar of Lord Vishnu.**
 
• Mohiniyattam reflects the theme of love and devotion, **where the dancer often plays the role of Mohini, who is the amorous and devoted heroine.**
 
• **Mohini, the divine enchantress, is often depicted as seductive, beautiful, and capable of mesmerizing those who she wishes to influence.**
 
• The dance form is characterized by graceful and gentle movements, **and it is traditionally performed solo by women.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 God
 Relation to Dance
 
 
 
 

 Kartikeya
 Kartikeya, also known as Murugan, is often associated with Tamil folk dance forms like "Kavadi Attam," performed in honour of him.
 
 

 Shiva
 
 
Shiva, as Nataraja, is known as the Lord of Dance.

 
The dance form Tandava symbolizes the cosmic cycles of creation and destruction, as well as the daily rhythm of birth and death.

 
One of the classical Indian dances, Bharatanatyam, draws heavily from the dance poses held by the cosmic dancer Shiva.

 
 
 

 Krishna
 Krishna, an avatar of Vishnu, is associated with the classical dance form of Kathak and the folk dance form of Raas Leela or Raas Lilas, which portray his early life, love-play with Radha, and his flirtatious interactions with the Gopis.

questions.question: In which of the soil conservation methods in the coastal and dry regions, rows of trees are planted to check the wind movement to protect soil cover?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shelter belts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shelter belts are rows of** trees and shrubs planted to protect soil from wind erosion, particularly in coastal and arid regions.**
 
• These tree lines reduce wind **speed across the ground and thereby decrease the wind's ability to lift and carry soil particles away, combating wind erosion effectively.**
 
• Apart from reducing **wind erosion, shelter belts also offer additional benefits like providing habitat for wildlife, sequestering carbon, and enhancing the landscape's aesthetics.**
 
• This method is quite common in **flat, dry regions where wind erosion is a major issue, such as parts of North America, Africa, and Asia.**
 
• Shelter belts can take the form of **single or multiple rows of trees or shrubs,** depending on the severity of the wind erosion problem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulching:**

 
 
• Mulching involves covering the soil surface with a layer of organic or inorganic material **(like straw, leaves, compost, or plastic sheets).**
 
• This technique **retains soil moisture, suppresses weed growth, and can also prevent soil erosion by reducing the impact of raindrops on the soil surface.**
 
 
 
• **Rock Dam:**
 
 
• Rock dams are barriers built across channels, gullies, or small waterways using rocks.
 
• They slow down the flow of water, reduce its erosive power and trap sediments.
 
• **This technique is commonly used in mountainous regions or areas prone to flash floods and gully erosion.**
 
 
 
• **Contour Barriers:**
 
 
• **​**Contour barriers are physical barriers like **stones, vegetation, or soil bunds constructed along the contours of a slope.**
 
• **They slow down water runoff, promote water infiltration, and reduce soil erosion by water.**
 
• This method is typically used on sloping land in both farming and forestry.

questions.question: _______ is the chemical process in which different types of chemical reactions are involved in controlling the living state of the cells in an organism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metabolism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metabolism **is the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions in organisms.
 
• It involves various chemical reactions that occur in the cells to maintain the living state of the organism.
 
• These reactions are organized into **metabolic pathways, in which one chemical is transformed through a series of steps into another chemical, by a sequence of enzymes.**
 
• **Metabolism is divided into two categories:** catabolism, the breaking down of compounds to produce** energy; and anabolism, the construction of compounds, which uses energy.**
 
• Metabolism involves the transfer of energy from one form to another, and the conversion of substances into other substances in various metabolic pathways.
 
• The rate of metabolism affects the amount of** food and the type of food that an organism will need; it also affects the physical characteristics of an organism, such as size and shape.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Transportation
 
 
In the context of biology, transportation refers to the movement of substances like nutrients, oxygen, and waste products to and from cells in the body.

 
This can occur through processes such as diffusion, osmosis, or active transport.

 
 
 

 Respiration
 
 
This is the process by which organisms exchange gases with their environment.

 
In cellular respiration, oxygen is used to break down glucose, providing energy in the form of ATP and producing carbon dioxide as a byproduct.

 
 
 

 Excretion
 
 
This is the process by which waste products of metabolism and other non-useful materials are eliminated from an organism.

 
In humans, this primarily occurs via the kidneys, which filter blood and produce urine.
